<!-- pr-reviewer: 26e8610e5a6cbc7feb4ff5c88e717d782f502b75 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- `frameWord` (assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:619-631) maps G54-G57 unchanged, G58 -> G505, G59 -> G506, and any other word that `frameOf` does not resolve is refused by name through `msg` (counted warning). Both call sites go through it: the section's `WorkOffset` parameter (:302) and the probe result (:657).
- Behaviour check against the public 840D sl documentation (behaviour only): settable zero offsets are G54-G57 and G505-G599; G58/G59 are axial programmable offsets that select no frame. The mapping matches.
- Probe index arithmetic: `frameOf` gives G54-G57 -> 1..4 and G505..G599 -> n-500, so G505 -> 5 and G506 -> 6. That is the same 1-based `$P_UIFR[n,..]` convention offsets 1-4 already used, so setting offset 6 writes `$P_UIFR[6,axis,TR/FI]`. The new probe_dialects test asserts that line.
- Scope is tight: only sinumerik.cps, two tests and a decision file. No other post, no golden and no snapshot changes.
- The replaced probe_dialects test is stronger. It used to pin the refusal. It now pins the written frame-6 line and that no G58/G59 word is emitted. The new `sinumerik_work_offsets.rs` pins offsets 1-6 -> G54..G57, G505, G506 with zero warnings, and refuses G53 by name.
- Decision file at docs/decisions/934-sinumerik-g505.md. Commit subjects are conventional. Body ends `Fixes #934`.

**Local results** (trial-merged with current upstream/main, clean merge, no conflicts; macOS, worktree's own target/, sccache)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `sinumerik_work_offsets` | 2 passed |
| `probe_dialects` | 13 passed |
| `posting` | 17 passed |
| `conformance` | 6 passed |
| `golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| `camcraft-post` (all targets) | all ok, 0 failed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-post --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app` on the two touched test binaries `-D warnings` | clean |

I did not run app lib tests or `clippy --all-targets` on camcraft-app, because main is red there (#1146); that is not this PR's doing. I could not run a simulator (Hub does not run Sinumerik).

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The probe re-selects `wcsWord`, the section's active frame (:668), not the frame just written. So "re-selects G506" in the PR text and decision file only holds when the active offset is also 6. In the test case (active G54, writing frame 6) it re-selects G54. That is existing behaviour and harmless, but the wording is loose.
2. The PR body has no `Changelog:` line (AGENTS.md); add one (this changes posted output) or the cut will have to derive it.
3. #931 (and the stacked #1101/#1113/#1124) will take over this mapping; `frameWord` should move into it cleanly, as the decision file says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
